title: Flow Control Power Comparator
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: Industrial and Commercial Fans: Flow Control
description: Prediction-challenge line chart comparing the illustrative shaft power of an outlet damper, variable inlet vanes and speed control from 50% to 100% airflow, with an airflow selector that reports the powers and savings at any 5% step.

educational.topic: Flow control methods and fan shaft power
learningObjectives: Differentiate outlet dampers, variable inlet vanes and speed control by the shaft power each needs at reduced airflow, correctly ranking the three methods and estimating the savings gap at a stated airflow between 50% and 100% of design.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal challenges followed by guided exploration
keyQuestions: At 80% airflow, which method uses the least power, and how much does it save compared with an outlet damper?
At 70% airflow, which method uses the least power, and how much does it save compared with an outlet damper?
At 50% airflow, which method uses the least power, and how much does it save compared with an outlet damper?
commonMisconceptions: Closing a damper to half flow cuts power roughly in half.
All flow-control methods save about the same energy.
Inlet vanes save as much as speed control.
Power falls in proportion to airflow when speed is reduced, rather than with roughly the cube of the airflow.
assessmentOpportunities: Three prediction challenges (80%, 70%, 50% airflow), two attempts each; correct when the ranking matches and the saving is within 3 percentage points. Mastery is 3 of 3.

dataProvenance: Speed-control values follow the ideal fan-law cube relation. Outlet damper and inlet vane values are illustrative values written for this chapter, not Twin City Fan test data; the ordering is supported by FanPedia pp. 145, 182, 183, 188.
